why: The answer depends on the outside-to-inside order produced by secondary growth in a woody dicot stem - phellem, secondary cortex (phelloderm), secondary phloem, then wood.
note: Topic gap: this chapter has no 'Secondary Growth' topic (vascular cambium, cork cambium/periderm, annual rings) and no 'Unspecified Topic' row, so the dicot stem topic was the closest home. Secondary growth is a high-yield NEET area and deserves its own topic.
